source_evidence.anchor: Original Samplinglib supplement: Quadratic variation of a finite predictable diffusion row. Exact assumptions and formula below.
source_evidence.statement: The compensated sum of the squares of actual diffusion-row increments is in L² on each dyadic grid and converges to zero in mean square.
assumptions: All coordinates are from one Euclidean Brownian driver with the stated filtration.
Every row coefficient is strongly measurable at its cell’s left endpoint, in L⁴, and subject to one uniform fourth-moment bound.
The coordinate type is finite. The horizon may be zero.
source_evidence.boundary: The coefficients are the specified grid rows. A continuous approximation has separate integrability and convergence obligations.

steps.title: Control the product weights
steps.mathematical_move: The average of two fourth powers bounds the square of the product. This gives the L² domain and the required uniform second moments.
steps.assessment: The formula and explanation implement the current proof move under the stated assumptions.

steps.title: Apply the diagonal and mixed results
steps.mathematical_move: The diagonal subtracts the elapsed time; distinct coordinates use the actual mixed increment product.
steps.assessment: The formula and explanation implement the current proof move under the stated assumptions.

steps.title: Expand the actual row square
steps.mathematical_move: Expanding the square and the compensator gives the finite sum over all ordered coordinate pairs.
steps.assessment: The formula and explanation implement the current proof move under the stated assumptions.

steps.title: Transfer the finite-sum limit
steps.mathematical_move: Each pair sum is square integrable and its squared expectation tends to zero. The square of the whole sum is bounded by the number of pairs times the sum of squares.
